subject: QuantumBridge: SLA disruption — stabilization sprint and exec commitments
messages:
From: Amanda Rios <amanda.rios@quantumbridge.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops@quantumbridge.com
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Severe latency + errors this morning — immediate help needed

Vanessa,

We saw a significant degradation starting ~08:45 ET this morning: 5-10x increased 95th percentile latency, a spike in 500 errors around our burst window, and effective throughput dropped by ~40% for our live checkout flow. Attached is a short timeline and sample traces.

This is impacting our checkout success rate and revenue. Our ops team toggled a rate limit and rerouted a portion of traffic to a fallback model, which helped, but we still see elevated errors. Can we get an exec-level readout and a concrete stabilization plan today? We need committed owners and ETA to restore SLA.

Thanks — Amanda
Amanda Rios
Head of Platform Engineering, QuantumBridge
attachments: quantumbridge_chain-of-events.xlsx (spreadsheet, 92KB)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Severe latency + errors this morning — immediate help needed

Amanda — thanks for the heads up and for the timeline. I pulled the on-call and engineering leads onto a call (09:40 ET) — attaching the short-term stabilization checklist we ran and the owners we've assigned so far. Immediate notes:

- We saw evidence of a KV cache warmup regression and an interaction with a recent quantized model build that increased memory pressure on a subset of dedicated hosts.
- Temporary mitigations applied: circuit-breaker for the largest clients, fallback routing to a slightly older model variant, and conservative autoscaling to add capacity to the dedicated pool.

Next steps we proposed on the call (short window):
1) 90-min stabilization sprint (owner: Marcus Lin) — aim to restore 95th P99 latency and drop 500s to <0.1% for checkout flow.
2) Deeper RCA and fix (owner: Kimberly Park) — target patch for quantization mismatch and kernel fallback by EOD+2.
3) Exec readout + credit discussion (owner: Vanessa Ortiz) — I will propose an acknowledgement and a one-time credit while we work through the fix.

We have an internal escalation doc live; will share a consolidated plan in ~2 hours. Thanks for patience — we understand the customer impact.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Team — notes + assigned actions from the 09:40 call. This email is the canonical action tracker for the stabilization sprint and the subsequent RCA. Keep replies minimal; update the tracker link and call out blockers.

Incident summary (short): 
- Root symptoms: elevated 95/99 latency, increased 500/timeout rates, and sustained throughput reduction during burst window.
- Probable causes observed: (a) new quantized model build introduced a kernel-path that causes KV cache thrash at high concurrency; (b) autoscaling thresholds were too conservative for the observed request spike; (c) a small fraction of hosts hit an OOM leading to cascading retries.

Stabilization sprint (owner: Marcus Lin) — 11:30–13:00 ET today- Tasks:
  * Force-roll fallback to model v-202704 (already 60% traffic routed) — Marcus
  * Expand dedicated pool by adding 4x smaller instances and temporarily increase max concurrency per host — Ops (Grace)
  * Apply temporary per-client concurrency caps for heavy customers — Marcus
  * Enable aggressive KV cache prewarm for checkout prefix and reduce shard-level locking — Kimberly
  * Monitor and abort if error-rate rises after any change; maintain rollback runbook — Vanessa

RCA build (owner: Kimberly Park) — due EOD Jun 6, 2027- Tasks:
  * Reproduce locally with quantized build + high concurrency harness; capture kernel-level traces.
  * Implement kernel fallback to safe path when memory pressure > X% and publish patch.
  * Update compilation heuristics to avoid the problematic kernel selection for sequences < 256 tokens.

Customer-facing commitments (owner: Vanessa Ortiz)- Items:
  * Exec readout scheduled Jun 4, 16:00 ET with Ethan Cole and Amanda Rios — I will run the slide deck and the timeline.
  * One-time credit proposal to be shared during readout (prelim: 10% of monthly invoice for affected window)
  * Weekly progress updates until closure.

Please update the shared tracker when tasks begin/completed: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-stabilization-plan

Vanessa

Subject: QuantumBridge — RCA delivered, patch rolled to canary, closure notes

Vanessa / team / Amanda — final update from engineering: 

RCA summary:
- Primary root cause: a recent quantized compilation selected an optimized kernel path that, under high concurrency with small-sequence traffic patterns, caused excessive KV cache evictions and transient memory pressure on a subset of dedicated hosts. The transient pressure triggered OOMs that led to retries and amplified latency/error symptoms.
- Contributing factors: autoscaler thresholds were tuned for average throughput, not high concurrency short-burst patterns; lack of a specific alert for kernel-selection anomalies.

What we did:
- Rolled a kernel-fallback patch (v20270608-kf1) to canary (10%) at 09:00 ET today; no regressions observed in canary's metrics over 6 hours.
- Adjusted compilation heuristics to avoid selecting the problematic kernel for sequences < 256 tokens.
- Implemented a KV prewarm for checkout prefixes and adjusted lock granularity to reduce thrash.
- Increased autoscale sensitivity for short-burst windows and added a synthetic load test to our CI to catch regressions.

Outcome and KPIs:
- Canary: 95th latency normalized to baseline; 500-rate <0.02% across test traffic.
- Production gradual rollout scheduled Jun 9 02:00–04:00 ET with automated rollback if errors exceed 0.1% for 15m.

Closure items / next steps:
- Formal post-incident report (full timeline, logs, and annotated trace deck) will be delivered by Jun 10 (owner: Kimberly Park).
- Vanessa to finalize credit note and confirm with Amanda by Jun 9.
- Ops (Grace) to run a capacity rehearse exercise with QuantumBridge on Jun 12 (owner: Grace O'Connor).

Amanda — we appreciate the partnership here. Let us know if you want the post-incident deck earlier; we can fast-track it.

Kimberly Park
Director, Inference Engineering, Redwood Inference
